notes: Hex fields are raw bytes. *_base64 fields are standard base64; fragments are base64url without padding.
fragment starts with the share kind byte and burn_fragment with the burn kind byte; each must be refused where the other is expected.
Encryption tests must use the manifest string exactly as given, not re-serialise it.
Argon2 memory (m) is in KiB. pass_key is the 32-byte Argon2id output.
Decryption tests must recover text and files exactly; reject cases must fail for the stated reason.

inputs.text: Two attachments. Second file name is UTF-8. 🔐

expected.manifest: {"v":1,"text":"Two attachments. Second file name is UTF-8. 🔐","files":[{"name":"notes.txt","type":"text/plain","size":18},{"name":"résumé.png","type":"image/png","size":1208}]}

reject.name: tag-tampered
reject.reason: last chunk tag fails to authenticate

reject.name: wrapped-ek-tampered
reject.reason: wrapped_EK fails to unwrap in direct mode; the client would prompt for a passphrase that does not exist

reject.name: truncated
reject.reason: length matches no valid padded size; the server refuses it and the client's final chunk fails to authenticate

reject.name: argon-m-below-bounds
reject.reason: argon_m below the client bound; reject before running the KDF

reject.name: argon-m-above-bounds
reject.reason: argon_m above the client bound; reject before running the KDF

reject.name: argon-t-above-bounds
reject.reason: argon_t above the client bound; reject before running the KDF

reject.name: last-flag-missing
reject.reason: the final chunk was sealed without the last flag, so it fails to authenticate as the final chunk; this is how a truncated stream is detected

reject.name: payload-len-too-large
reject.reason: payload_len exceeds bucket - 4; reject after decryption
